fieldissues.issue: The title states that DHS spied on groups as an established fact, while the medium attributes the claim and says the allegations remain unadjudicated.

proposedchanges.title: Court Filing Alleges DHS Monitored Minnesota Protest Groups
proposedchanges.description_long: Add a distinct long explanation that attributes the monitoring details to the defense filing and linked report, names the 18-group chart and alleged methods, and states that the allegations and legality remain unresolved.

evidencebasis: The World Socialist Web Site article, assigned packet, and current medium describe allegations from a court filing and explicitly say they remain unadjudicated. The latest merged entry has no long description.
notes: Keep the category and topic tags tied to the allegation and avoid stating that unlawful surveillance was established.

fieldissues.issue: “Renovation” does not match the descriptions’ $400 million ballroom construction project at the demolished East Wing site.
“National Security Violations” treats the administration’s stated rationale as the event; the dispute concerns construction and environmental review.
D. John Sauer is tagged but is not named in the assigned packet or latest descriptions.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Seeks Supreme Court Approval to Resume White House Ballroom Construction

evidencebasis: The Briefs.co article and latest descriptions identify a ballroom project, an environmental-review dispute, and a Supreme Court request. They do not identify an actual national-security violation or name Sauer in the text.
notes: The medium and long distinguish the petition from a ruling and retain the reported $400 million cost.

fieldissues.issue: “Plot to Seize Elections” presents an inflammatory characterization as fact, while the linked article describes legal and legislative obstacles to specific election changes.

proposedchanges.title: Trump Administration Faces Court and Congressional Obstacles to 2026 Election Changes

evidencebasis: The Independent article and latest descriptions report court losses, legislative resistance, and a hypothetical emergency-power remark. They do not establish a plot to seize elections.
notes: The long distinguishes completed court rulings from a possible emergency action; the topic tags identify the reported election measures.

fieldissues.issue: The title states “constitutional dictatorship” as fact, while the descriptions attribute it to essayist Mark Danner’s political interpretation.
Mark Danner is named as the essayist but is missing from people_tags.
New York Review of Books is tagged as an event organization although it is the essay publisher.

proposedchanges.title: Mark Danner Argues Trump Is Building a “Constitutional Dictatorship”

evidencebasis: The New York Review of Books essay and latest descriptions attribute the phrase to Danner’s interpretation. The current title removes that attribution, and the organization tag identifies only the publisher.
notes: The medium and long appropriately describe the source as an essay and distinguish its characterization from a court finding.

fieldissues.issue: “The Last Trump Elections” is vague and does not tell readers that the source is Ian Bremmer’s forecast about the 2026 midterms.
Joe Biden and Kamala Harris are not named in the descriptions; Ian Bremmer is named but missing from people_tags.
EL PAÍS is tagged as an event organization although it is the opinion-piece publisher.
The final sentence discusses what the linked piece does not claim rather than ending with Bremmer’s forecast.

proposedchanges.title: Ian Bremmer Predicts Trump Will Challenge 2026 Midterm Results but Not Change Them
proposedchanges.description_long: Remove the final sentence beginning “The linked piece does not claim.” Keep the explicit attribution that the election outcome is a forecast, not a verified result.

evidencebasis: The EL PAÍS opinion article and latest text identify Bremmer’s predictions about the November 2026 midterms. The current title omits that attribution, and the tags include unmentioned people and the publisher.
notes: The topic tags and election category fit a clearly attributed forecast about election administration.
